children: The CAC 40 index dropped nearly 1% to below 8,050 on Tuesday, extending losses from the previous session to hit a four-month low, as rising oil prices and global bond yields weighed on sentiment.
Oil prices continued to climb, with Brent crude rising above $107 per barrel after attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, raising inflation concerns and expectations for further rate hikes.
Higher yields further weighed on equities after the US 10-year Treasury yield reached 5%.
Locally, France’s final inflation readings showed annual consumer prices accelerated to 2.4% in August from 2.1% in July, reaching a three-month high.
Luxury stocks led the downturn, pressured by weaker Chinese demand and reduced access to the Middle East travel hub.
Luxury giants LVMH dropped 2.2%, while Hermes fell 1.3%.
In contrast, top gainers were Capgemini (6.6%), Dassault Systemes (5%) and TP (4.1%).

title: French Stocks Hit 4-Month Low
